title: ZIKR SYMPHONIC METAL
genre: Neo-Sacred Zikr / Symphonic Metal / Progressive Metal / Neoclassical Metal
description: A 19-movement Neo-Sacred Zikr cycle where a single sacred utterance, HÛ, rises from breath and silence into monumental choirs, symphonic orchestra, pipe organ and progressive neoclassical metal.
story:
ZIKR SYMPHONIC METAL opens a new chapter within Berk Köksal’s Neo-Sacred Zikr universe. Across nineteen interconnected works, the album is built around a single sacred utterance: HÛ. Rather than multiplying words, the music explores how one sound can carry different spiritual states — breath, mercy, surrender, awakening, devotion, ascension, majesty, unity, eternity and return.

The musical journey repeatedly moves from intimacy toward immensity. A fragile female voice, breath, silence, sacred choir, strings and organ gradually expand into brass, timpani, bass, drums, distorted guitars and virtuosic neoclassical solos. The classical world does not disappear when the metal enters; choir, orchestra, organ and guitars continue together as parts of the same act of remembrance.

Metal is not used here as an expression of anger. Its weight and power represent divine majesty and the overwhelming scale of creation. The choir is not decoration, the orchestra is not a background layer, and the guitar is not merely a vehicle for virtuosity. Every musical element serves the same center: zikr.

The nineteen pieces are conceived not simply as separate songs, but as movements in a single spiritual cycle. The Breath begins with the most intimate human element, while the later works expand through surrender, evidence, instinct, awakening, the path, devotion, ascension, divine majesty, the throne, infinity, universal unity and eternity. Miracle & Return closes the journey by returning to the point from which it began, now transformed by everything that came before.

The central idea of ZIKR SYMPHONIC METAL is simple: the utterance does not change, but the world of sound around it does. One breath becomes a choir; the choir becomes an orchestra; the orchestra becomes symphonic metal; and all of them finally return to HÛ.

title: ZIKR JAZZ
genre: Neo-Sacred Zikr / Spiritual Jazz / Modal Jazz / Sacred Music
description: An intimate Neo-Sacred Zikr album where spiritual jazz, warm acoustic instrumentation and the beautiful names of GOD meet in quiet remembrance.
story:
ZIKR JAZZ is one of the most introspective, elegant and melodic works in Berk Köksal’s Neo-Sacred Zikr universe. The album reflects upon the beautiful names of GOD and the divine attributes found in the Quran through the free harmonic language of jazz.

Within the Neo-Sacred Zikr approach, each album represents a different spiritual atmosphere. Zikr Symphony embodies grandeur, ZIKR ROCK expresses power, ZIKR RAP carries rhythm, Classical Chorus centers on monumental choirs, and Zikr-i Batin explores the silent remembrance of the heart. ZIKR JAZZ, by contrast, takes the form of a sincere prayer offered in the stillness of the night. Simplicity is placed above spectacle, depth above loudness, and submission above technical display.

The female vocal heard throughout the album is not merely a performer, but a bearer of remembrance. Fingerstyle hollow-body jazz guitar, warm grand piano, double bass, brushed drums, flugelhorn, tenor and soprano saxophones, together with occasional ney and oud textures, create a breathing sound world around the voice. Each instrument responds in support of the zikr; none is allowed to stand before the names of GOD.

The lyrics are shaped around the beautiful names of GOD, divine names mentioned in the Quran, attributes appearing at the ends of verses, and expressions of remembrance. Repetition is not used merely as a musical device; it represents the heart remembering the same truth again and again. With every return, the harmony changes and the emotion deepens, while the center remains unchanged: glorifying GOD.

Musically, the album draws inspiration from modern modal jazz, spiritual jazz and classical jazz harmony. Maj7, maj9, min9, add9, 6/9 and suspended chords, melodic minor colors, diminished transitions and subtle chromatic movement create a warm, natural and deeply human sound. Improvisations are deliberately restrained, allowing silence itself to become part of the music.

Each piece centers on a different name of GOD or on divine attributes that appear together in the Quran. The journey begins with Wallahu Azizun Hakim and moves through themes of forgiveness, mercy, knowledge, wisdom, power, light and the oneness of GOD, before reaching a peaceful conclusion with Dhul-Jalali Wal-Ikram. The album invites the listener not only to hear music, but also to reflect, give thanks, remember GOD and contemplate His names.

ZIKR JAZZ is the first expression of jazz within the Neo-Sacred Zikr universe. It does not approach jazz merely as a language of entertainment, but as the musical expression of sincere supplication, silent remembrance and heartfelt submission.
